# Adversarial corpus for the DomUtils.serializeNode / getNodeBytes oracle.
#
# gen/SerializeOracle.java reads this file, reproduces DomUtils.serializeNode(Node) and
# DomUtils.getNodeBytes(Node) VERBATIM on every (document, selected node) pair, and writes
# goldens.txt. serialize_oracle_test.go replays the same corpus through the Go port and
# demands byte equality.
#
# Record syntax - one record per "case" line, keys in any order after it:
#
#   case <name>                unique, no spaces
#   parse <escaped text>       source document, parsed from its UTF-8 bytes
#   parseb64 <base64>          source document, parsed from these raw bytes
#   build <escaped DSL>        document built programmatically (see below)
#   sel <path>                 node to serialize; omitted/"." selects the Document
#   divergence <text>          this case is known NOT to agree with Java; the text says why.
#                              The Go side must still refuse it somewhere, and the golden is
#                              not compared. May be repeated to continue the text.
#
# Escapes in <escaped text>: \\ \n \r \t \s (space) \uXXXX (one UTF-16 code unit).
# The token ~ on its own means the empty string.
#
# sel is a dot-separated list of child indices from the Document node ("0.2" = third child
# of the first child). A trailing "@<qname>" selects that attribute of the addressed
# element instead.
#
# build DSL: ops separated by ";", arguments by spaces. "-" is a null namespace URI.
#   e <ns> <qname>     createElementNS(ns, qname), appended and pushed
#   a <ns> <qname> <v> setAttributeNS on the current element
#   ap <name> <v>      setAttribute on the current element (null namespaceURI)
#   t <text>           appendChild(createTextNode(text))
#   c <text>           appendChild(createComment(text))
#   d <text>           appendChild(createCDATASection(text))
#   p <target> <data>  appendChild(createProcessingInstruction(target, data))
#   /                  pop back to the parent
#
# A "build" given alongside a "parse" is DOM surgery on the parsed document, starting at
# its document element - which is the shape XAdES signing has: parse, graft, serialize.
#
# There is deliberately no op for Document.createElement(name). Xerces answers null to
# getLocalName() for such a node, and DOM2TO's namespace fixup tests exactly that - so a
# createElement child of an element in a default namespace does NOT get xmlns="" while a
# createElementNS(null, name) child does. internal/xmldom has no representation for an
# element without a local name, and the one call site upstream
# (InternallyDetachedSignatureBuilder's container element) is a fresh document's root,
# where no default namespace is in scope and the two behave identically.

# --------------------------------------------------------------- structure and selection
case doc-simple
parse <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><r><a/></r>
sel .

# ------------------------------------------------ declared-encoding alias table
# One case per encoding-name spelling internal/xmldom's decodeSource accepts. Xerces reports
# getXmlEncoding() verbatim (probed), DomUtils.serializeNode copies it onto
# OutputKeys.ENCODING, and that one property decides three things at once: the text of the
# declaration (Encodings.convertJava2MimeEncoding), which characters are written literally
# rather than as decimal character references (EncodingInfo.isInEncoding), and the charset the
# bytes are actually written in. The payload carries one ASCII, one Latin-1, one BMP and one
# astral character so all three are visible in every row.
case enc-00
# encoding="UTF-8"
parseb64 PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iVVRGLTgiPz48ciB2PSJhJiN4ZTk7JiN4NGUyZDsmI3gxZjYwMDsiPmImI3hlOTsmI3g0ZTJkOyYjeDFmNjAwOzwvcj4=
sel .

case enc-01
# encoding="utf-8"
parseb64 PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0idXRmLTgiPz48ciB2PSJhJiN4ZTk7JiN4NGUyZDsmI3gxZjYwMDsiPmImI3hlOTsmI3g0ZTJkOyYjeDFmNjAwOzwvcj4=
sel .

divergence Xerces refuses the encoding name "latin-1" outright - it is not an IANA-registered
divergence alias of ISO-8859-1 - so Java never reaches the serializer. internal/xmldom.decodeSource
divergence accepts it and the failure only surfaces when the output encoding is looked up. Recorded,
divergence not fixed: narrowing the parser is a change to Parse, not to the serializer.

# ------------------------------------------- getNodeBytes' lossy charset round trip
# getNodeBytes does new String(bytes) and then getBytes(), both in the platform default
# charset - UTF-8 since JEP 400. When serializeNode wrote something other than UTF-8 the
# round trip is lossy, and how lossy depends on java.nio.charset.UTF_8's malformed-input
# lengths: a truncated multi-byte sequence collapses to ONE U+FFFD while three separately
# invalid bytes become three. Attribute values are the vehicle because they are the one
# place the serializer leaves C1 bytes unescaped.
case latin1-utf8-decoder-subparts
parseb64 PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iSVNPLTg4NTktMSI/PjxyIGE9IumpIiBiPSLDqSIgYz0i4ICAIiBkPSLtoIAiIGU9Iv/+IiBmPSL0kICAIiBnPSLwn5giLz4=
sel .

case latin1-utf8-decoder-tail
parseb64 PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIiBlbmNvZGluZz0iSVNPLTg4NTktMSI/PjxyIGE9InjpIi8+
sel .

# ------------------------------------------- declarations the serializer drops entirely
# Both of these are internal/xmlc14n corpus documents. A redundant redeclaration of a
# prefix already bound to the same URI, and any declaration of a prefix beginning with
# "xml", are swallowed by NamespaceMappings.pushNamespace - so a serialize/parse round
# trip does NOT preserve the physical canonical form, in Java exactly as here.
case c14n-corpus-ns-superfluous
parse <r xmlns:p="urn:1" Id="r"><p:c xmlns:p="urn:1" Id="c"><p:d xmlns:p="urn:1" Id="d"/></p:c></r>
sel .

case c14n-corpus-ns-superfluous-subtree
parse <r xmlns:p="urn:1" Id="r"><p:c xmlns:p="urn:1" Id="c"><p:d xmlns:p="urn:1" Id="d"/></p:c></r>
sel 0.0

case c14n-corpus-ns-xml-prefix
parse <r xmlns:xml="http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace" Id="r"><c Id="c" xml:lang="en"><t Id="t"/></c></r>
sel .

case c14n-corpus-xml-prefix-subtree
parse <r xmlns:xml="http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace" Id="r"><c Id="c" xml:lang="en"><t Id="t"/></c></r>
sel 0.0

# ------------------------------------------------- systematic character sweep (UTF-8)
# One case per (interesting code point x node kind). This is where the escaping tables,
# the C0/C1 rule, the XML-1.0 validity check, the CDATA character-reference break-out and
# the comment/PI raw-write paths all get exercised against the real serializer rather than
# against a reading of it. Cases whose golden is ERROR are the ones Java refuses.

build e - r; t a\u0001b

# ------------------------------------ supplementary characters written without escaping
# Text and attribute values turn every supplementary character into a decimal character
# reference, so the only way one reaches the byte writer literally is inside CDATA, a
# comment, a processing instruction or a name. Which writer that is depends on the exact
# spelling of the encoding, and they do not agree.
case astral-raw-03FFFF
build e - r; d a\uD8BF\uDFFFb
sel 0

case astral-raw-040000
build e - r; d a\uD8C0\uDC00b
sel 0

case astral-raw-040001
build e - r; d a\uD8C0\uDC01b
sel 0

case astral-raw-07FFFF
build e - r; d a\uD9BF\uDFFFb
sel 0

case astral-raw-080000
build e - r; d a\uD9C0\uDC00b
sel 0

case astral-raw-0E0100
build e - r; d a\uDB40\uDD00b
sel 0

case astral-raw-10FFFF
build e - r; d a\uDBFF\uDFFFb

# --------------------------- characters the declared encoding cannot carry, after surgery
# Each of these parses a document in some encoding and then grafts a comment, a processing
# instruction, a CDATA section and a text node carrying characters outside it. The text
# node escapes them, the CDATA section escapes only what its own rule rejects, and the
# comment and the processing instruction hand them to the byte writer unescaped - so this
# is where the writer's substitution behaviour, which differs between spellings of the
# same encoding, becomes observable.
case graft-00
# encoding="UTF-8"

build c aéb中c😀d; p t eéf中g; d héi中j; t kél中m

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- ISO-8859-2 (Latin-2)
# The only single-byte charset beyond Latin-1 the upstream XAdES corpus declares -
# validation/Signature-X-HU_MIC-1.xml and validation/BaselineBWithCertificateValues.xml both
# do. Every one of the 96 characters in the top half is round-tripped, in text and in an
# attribute value, so a wrong entry in the table cannot hide; the out-of-charset rows pin
# that a character Latin-2 cannot carry becomes a DECIMAL character reference in text and in
# an attribute and a '?' in a comment or a processing instruction; and the alias rows pin
# which spellings Encodings.properties rewrites in the declaration and which it echoes back
# unchanged (probed against OpenJDK 21: ISO8859_2, ISO8859-2 and iso-8859-2 all become
# "ISO-8859-2"; latin2, csISOLatin2, ISO_8859-2 and cp912 do not).

sel .
